the use of tamoxifen or raloxifense for the chemoprevention of breast cancer in high-risk women results in the following: (i) a 50% reduction in the diagnosis of invasive breast cancer and a 50% increase in the diagnosis of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) after 5 years of therapy with tamoxifen and a 38% reduction in the risk of invasive breast cancer after 5 years with raloxifine; (ii

the use of tamoxifen for breast cancer chemoprevention has been associated with a 50% relative reduction in the risk of invasive breast cancer and a 70% relative reduction in noninvasive breast cancer.

(1) tamoxifen and raloxifence reduce the diagnosis of invasive breast cancer by about 50% and 38% respectively, (2) the benefits of these drugs are sustained after 5 years of therapy, and (3) the drugs have a low toxicity profile, including low risks of endometrial cancer, stroke, and thromboembolic events.

we have to be very careful about what we call "chemoprevention," because it is not a single entity.
